assignment_rationale: A5: direct same-family Polymarket evidence of concentrated informed trading plus broader corporate-announcement evidence. C5/S5: frozen ARGOS panel has 117 event contracts with PIT cutoffs. P4: pre-cutoff tape and dense probability trajectories are reproducible for 115/117. L3: repeated pre-cutoff trade/probability histories supported feature construction, but no higher lifetime-volume anchor is claimed. I4: direct listed single-name mapping with material earnings-event evidence. R5: objective threshold semantics and 116/117 independent official reconstruction with 116/116 matches. T3: recurring pre-announcement/overnight diffusion is plausible, but a structural PM-first window was not proven. PIS7: heavily monitored scheduled environment. SCB1: recurring contracts are not primarily rumor-created. DEF2: high reproducibility with limited timing/missingness edge cases.

A3: Federal Reserve research documents informed positioning/order flow and pre-announcement price discovery. C4/L4/S4: manual review establishes >=50 recurring macro/Fed events, median lead >7d, all 50 reviewed events >$10k and >$100k lifetime volume. P2: event metadata are reproducible; family-wide PIT trade histories were not reconstructed in this audit. I3: liquid rates/index instruments provide a defensible tight asset set, though mapping is less single-name than corporate events. R5: policy decisions and official macro releases are mechanically/authoritatively resolved. T2: competing rates/equity markets observe public releases nearly simultaneously, so a structural PM-first window is not established. PIS10: extremely saturated scheduled forecasting environment. SCB0: recurring contracts systematically predate releases. DEF2: official outcomes and market structure are highly reproducible, with broad-asset mapping the main architecture trade-off.

A3: primary research documents informed options trading before FDA advisory meetings. C4/L2/S4: manual performance-blind review establishes >=50 independent FDA decision events, median lead >7d and repeated but heterogeneous liquidity. P2: event metadata are reproducible, while family-wide historical trade reconstruction remains incomplete. I4: specific sponsor equities can be materially exposed to binary product decisions. R4: authoritative FDA outcomes are usually objective, with product/label semantic edge cases. T2: pre-event information heterogeneity is supported, but PM-before-equity lead is not structurally demonstrated. PIS4: specialized but monitored. SCB2: many contracts predate decisions by weeks. DEF5: sparse/heterogeneous liquidity and asset/product mapping remain material research costs.

A4: merger-announcement informed-trading evidence is supported by multiple corporate-announcement studies. C3/L2/S3: manual review establishes >=25 corporate M&A announcement/acquisition events with long positive lead, but only moderate repeated liquidity. P2: reproducible event metadata exist; complete family trade histories are not yet audited. I3: many events map to a specific public acquirer/target, but private-company cases make mapping heterogeneous. R3: announcement/deal-occurrence rules are usually auditable but definitions and deadlines vary. T3: pre-announcement diffusion is economically plausible. PIS2: less standardized public forecasting than earnings/macro. SCB8: severe risk that contracts are created after public rumors. DEF5: heterogeneous mappings and rumor timing materially complicate PIT testing.

A2: primary evidence supports material corporate impact, but direct same-family informed-trading evidence is limited. I3/R3: some regulator/court outcomes map to affected firms and authoritative decisions. P2/T2: prediction-market metadata exist and pre-resolution uncertainty is plausible. The frozen targeted queries are contaminated by generic DOJ/FTC uses and manual review establishes only a lower bound of 6 relevant independent events; C/L/S remain unassigned because low discovery count cannot prove absence or gate failure.

A2: legal-event studies support heterogeneous case information and material effects but not a repeated PM-specific informed-trading mechanism. C2/L2/S2: manual review establishes 10 distinct adjudication/settlement events with positive lead and usable activity. P2: event metadata are reproducible. I2: the broad court/litigation family usually lacks a consistent specific tradeable asset; corporate cases are a narrower subset, so the frozen family fails the I>=3 gate. R3: authoritative outcomes exist but case semantics vary. T2: some pre-decision lead is plausible. DEF6 reflects case-by-case timing, resolution and asset-mapping burden.

A3: post-announcement completion uncertainty has primary evidence. I5: merger-spread completion gives the clearest near-mechanical single-name payoff linkage in the candidate set. R4: close/block/clearance outcomes are generally authoritative. T3: completion probability can evolve before final asset repricing. However targeted discovery manually establishes only a positive lower bound of 3 strict independent completion/clearance events; because the discovery method is incomplete, C/L/S are intentionally left unassigned rather than scored as failures.
